item.title: Alwaldend.com
item.description:
Alwaldend.com is the repository’s main website and documentation site. It uses Hugo with Docsy to publish project documentation on GitHub Pages.

Historical www architecture

This historical diagram preserves the former Proxmox unikernel deployment; see Deployment for the current website. The Mermaid source is authoritative; Bazel renders its light and dark SVGs.

Links

  • Source code: https://github.com/alwaldend/src/tree/master/projects/alwaldend.com
  • Github Pages repo: https://github.com/alwaldend/alwaldend.github.io
  • Hugo rules: ../../tools/rules_hugo

Features

  • Hugo site
  • Docsy, Bootstrap

The homepage, blog, documentation, and project pages share a flat monochrome theme with white and charcoal color modes, subtle borders, and system fonts. The navigation’s theme menu supports light, dark, and system preferences. Every page uses an “Al” SVG favicon outlined in Architects Daughter. Prose links are underlined, and keyboard focus uses a visible outline. Scrollbars are thin and muted; taxonomy links use small rounded labels shared with the project index. Documentation sidebars use plain action rows, uppercase group headings, compact wrapping taxonomy items, subtle hover and active backgrounds spanning the full tree row, and compact chevrons. Tree labels stay indented; chevrons expand branches independently of the row’s page link. Headings, search fields, code blocks, tables, and callouts follow the same typography and surface styles. Syntax highlighting uses CSS classes so code colors follow the active theme. Documentation Mermaid images use the same light/dark palette and follow the theme menu, including system preference. They use clean, rounded nodes and containers, smooth connectors, embedded sans-serif lettering, and Mermaid’s native Dagre layout, with bordered caption plates for edge labels and container titles. The mermaid_site_svg macro in pkg/mermaid/defs.bzl derives light/dark configurations from the shared Sass palette and renders both SVGs through the native Mermaid API without post-processing. The preset supplies caption styling through themeCSS and places titles on container borders with Mermaid’s subGraphTitleMargin setting. Compact node/rank spacing and the pinned renderer’s edgeSpacing option separate nested title plates. Package both outputs and reference the light .svg; Markdown and the SVG shortcode recognize its .dark.svg sibling. The site theme selects the visible image, and print always uses light. Historical blog diagrams retain their original files and presentation. New raster diagrams can use mermaid_site_webp from the same macro file to encode the native diagram with the site’s palette and sans-serif font for syndication and social previews. Set color_scheme = "dark" to select the dark palette; the default remains light. The homepage panel links to GitHub, GitLab, Blog, Docs, and the project index, followed by permanently visible, indented project links in title order. Each row shows its destination alongside its title; narrow screens place the destination below the title. The panel has space below the fixed header.

item.title: Anki as code
item.description:
Anki as code exports collections as protobuf-backed TOML, plans changes, and reconciles them through Anki’s native API. It accepts modern .colpkg archives containing collection.anki21b and offline collection databases such as collection.anki2. Keep Anki and other writers closed during export, state operations, apply, and build. Plan, config dump, and state dump use stdout; status and errors use stderr.

Configuration paths identify objects, similar to Terraform. Native IDs live in Anki and collection-backed state; note GUIDs remain Anki metadata. New files create new objects; explicit moves retain existing identities and review progress. Apply/build leave all configuration files unchanged. New notes and their note types can be created in the same apply, without generating or writing identities into source.

item.title: Anki as code
item.description:
Keep notes, decks, and settings in text files. Edit them with your usual tools, review a plan of the changes, and reconcile your Anki collection with the result.

How it works

  1. Export an existing collection to TOML. Each note keeps its named fields and generated-card deck assignments, with deck titles derived from directory names.
  2. Bind config paths to existing Anki objects with col state import. Export leaves the source collection unchanged and does not create or install state.
  3. Edit the text. Change fields and tags, move notes between decks, or create new notes identified by their configuration paths. Create note types and edit their fields, templates, CSS, and configuration.
  4. Inspect the plan, then apply it to an offline collection or build a new archive from the original.

Features

  • Named fields preserve Anki HTML and media references.
  • Collection-backed state and explicit moves preserve existing identities.
  • Plans show declared changes and known card assignments; Anki generates cards during apply.
  • Anki validates templates, generates cards, and rebuilds field caches.
  • Export writes configs only; state dump exports stored bindings separately.
  • State import binds independently written configs to existing objects.
  • Apply and build leave configurations unchanged; Anki owns IDs and GUIDs.
  • Note types, ordered fields, templates, CSS, and browser fonts are editable.
  • Existing scheduling and media remain in the collection.

Status

The CLI is in development. It supports modern collection archives and offline Anki collections supported by the pinned backend. Reconciliation preserves review history while retaining existing card scheduling. Scheduling presets remain unmanaged; media stays in the original archive.

item.title: Leetcode downloader
item.description:
This project exports LeetCode submissions and generates documentation from submission files using a CLI and Bazel rules. A Tampermonkey script provides a browser-based download path; direct CLI downloads are currently blocked by LeetCode bot protection.

Links

  • Source code: https://github.com/alwaldend/src/tree/master/projects/leetcode_downloader

Features

  • CLI and bzl code to generate submission docs
  • Tampermonkey script to download submissions
  • CLI to download submissions (Doesn’t work because of bot protection)

Usage

Generate submission from a submission file

bazel run //projects/leetcode_downloader -- \
    --submissions-file "${PWD}/out/submissions.json" \
    --root-dir "${PWD}" \
    generate

Help

Usage of flags:
  -base_url string
    	 (default "https://leetcode.com")
  -cookie string

  -limit uint
    	 (default 20)
  -offset uint

  -root-dir string
    	 (default "${PWD}")
  -submissions-file string

item.title: Renders
item.description:
This project owns reusable Blender assets, their controlling references, and acceptance evidence bound to exact candidate bytes. Maintained work uses the project OpenSpec workspace.

The Reimu Fumo work lives under assets/reimu_fumo/. Its reusable asset target will be added only after a candidate passes the visual, structural, animation, and exact-byte delivery gates in Reimu Fumo change. That change preserves the open outcome, blocked execution and original goal history.

Working candidates and intermediate renders belong under the repository-root out/reimu_fumo_finish/ directory. They are not accepted or durable merely because they exist there. A historical packet may move into the source tree only when exact bytes and provenance are verified and it is labeled with its actual rejected or accepted state.
